results.title: Bayesian Model Comparison Essentials
results.content: It involves evaluating the performance of different models to determine which one best explains the observed data. In this guide, we will explore the essential techniques and best practices for Bayesian model comparison, including Bayes factors, posterior predictive checks, and cross-validation techniques. The techniques covered in this guide will provide a comprehensive understanding of Bayesian model comparison, enabling researchers to make informed decisions when evaluating model performance. ## Bayes Factors for Model Comparison. Bayes factors are a popular method for comparing the performance of different models in Bayesian statistics. Bayes factors can be interpreted as the relative evidence provided by the data for one model over another. ### Interpretation of Bayes Factors for Model Comparison. While Bayes factors are a powerful tool for model comparison, they have some limitations and challenges. * Using Bayes factors in conjunction with other model comparison techniques, like posterior predictive checks. ## Posterior Predictive Checks for Model Evaluation. Posterior predictive checks (PPCs) are a technique used to evaluate the performance of a Bayesian model by comparing the observed data to data simulated from the posterior predictive distribution. ## Cross-Validation Techniques for Bayesian Models. Cross-validation is a technique used to evaluate the performance of a model by splitting the available data into training and testing sets. ### Types of Cross-Validation Techniques for Bayesian Models. * **Leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO-CV)**: This involves leaving out one observation at a time and evaluating the model's performance on the remaining data. * **K-fold cross-validation**: This involves splitting the data into $K$ folds and evaluating the model's performance on each fold. These tools provide efficient and reliable methods for performing cross-validation and evaluating model performance. By using techniques like Bayes factors, posterior predictive checks, and cross-validation, researchers can evaluate the performance of different models and identify the most suitable one for their data. Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Bayes factors are used to compare the relative evidence provided by the data for different models, while posterior predictive checks are used to evaluate the absolute fit of a single model to the data. ### Can I use Bayes factors with non-nested models?

results.title: Bayesian Model Comparison - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
results.content: Bayesian model comparison is defined as the process of selecting between nested or non-nested models by choosing the model with the highest posterior probability given the data, often utilizing the Bayes factor as a ratio of the likelihoods of the models. : A tutorial is provided on how to perform Bayesian model selection more efficiently based on approximate LOO methods which use approximate posterior inference and subsampling via the difference estimator. But, when doing Bayesian model comparison, the form of the prior is crucial because the Bayes factor integrates the likelihood function weighted by the prior distribution. Therefore, the posterior probabilities of the models, and the Bayes factors, can be extremely sensitive to the choice of prior distribution. When doing Bayesian model comparison, different forms of vague priors can yield very different Bayes factors. 128, for an example of a beta distribution with shape parameters less than 1.) Using a Haldane prior to express the anything's-possible model, the Bayes factor is. Unlike Bayesian model comparison, when doing Bayesian estimation of continuous parameters within models and using realistically large amounts of data, the posterior distribution on the continuous parameters is typically robust against changes in vague priors. For example, a random 10% of the data could inform the priors of the models, and the remaining 90% used for computing the Bayes factor in the model comparison. It is shown how Bayesian model selection can be scaled efficiently for big data via PSIS-LOO-CV in combination with approximate posterior inference and probability-proportional-to-size subsampling. We have now seen several examples of Bayesian approaches to assessing a null value, using a model-comparison approach or a parameter-estimation approach. Visualizing the Bayes’ factor as the ratio of posterior to prior probabilities within a narrow OPE helps us intuit the apparent contradictions between the conclusions of the model comparison and the parameter estimation. Next to hypothesis testing and parameter estimation, Bayesian model comparison is one of the major applications of the Bayesian approach, and the comparison of statistical models is an essential part of psychological research (Edwards et al., 1963; Gronau et al., 2019; Kruschke, 2015; Ly et al., 2016a, 2016b; Wagenmakers et al., 2010).

results.title: Bayesian Model Selection: An In-Depth Guide
results.content: Bayesian Model Selection: An In-Depth Guide Bayesian Model Selection: An In-Depth Guide Techniques and Metrics for Optimal Bayesian Models Sarah Lee AI generated o3-mini 8 min read· May 15, 2025 Photo by Diana Vargas on Unsplash * Widely Applicable Information Criterion (WAIC) * Using Stan for Model Comparison Bayesian model selection is a methodology for comparing different statistical models using Bayesian techniques. Rather than focusing solely on point estimates or p-values, Bayesian approaches incorporate prior knowledge and quantify uncertainty through the probability distribution of model parameters. In this guide, we walk through the key components of Bayesian model selection, including criteria for comparing models, practical steps in implementing these methods, and real-world case studies. We also provide insights into best practices in Bayesian model evaluation to help practitioners avoid common pitfalls and ensure responsible interpretation of results. In Bayesian contexts, k-fold cross-validation or leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO-CV) is used to estimate how well a model will perform on unseen data. Use the generated log-likelihood values to compute model evidence estimates and employ criteria such as WAIC or DIC. Real-world case studies help illustrate the practical application of Bayesian model selection. After fitting both models using MCMC and evaluating with WAIC and LOO-CV, one might find that even if Model B has a lower WAIC, the improvement may not justify the increased model complexity if the quadratic term is not statistically significant. After conducting PSIS-LOO or WAIC analysis, Model 2 might provide improved predictions but be more sensitive to the choice of priors. Adhering to best practices ensures robust application of Bayesian model selection methods. When interpreting model comparison results: * Be cautious of small differences in WAIC or LOO-CV scores. Bayesian model selection offers a robust framework for comparing models by integrating prior knowledge with observed data. From understanding Bayes factors and model evidence to implementing practical solutions in Stan and PyMC3, the techniques discussed in this guide provide a comprehensive toolkit for applied statisticians and machine learning practitioners. * Multiple criteria, including DIC, WAIC, and cross-validation methods, help balance model fit with complexity.
